claim: Section 224 of the House Armed Services Committee's Chairman's Mark of the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act (H.R. 8800, marked up May 21, 2026), titled "United States–Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative," directs the Secretary of Defense to designate a standing executive agent (per DoD Directive 5101.01) "responsible for synchronizing cooperative efforts between the United States and Israel, to expand and accelerate bilateral defense technology research, development, testing, evaluation, integration, and industrial cooperation" — including identifying "Israeli-origin technologies" for "integration into United States systems and programs of record" and establishing "United States-based co-production or manufacturing partnerships with Israeli industry." Subsection (b) lists ten cooperation domains, among them "(4) Artificial intelligence, quantum, machine learning, and autonomous systems" and "(8) Network integration, data fusion, and contested logistics." The section's text is lifted from the U.S.-Israel FUTURES Act (H.R. 7540 / S. 3855), introduced February 12, 2026 by Rep. Ronny Jackson (R-TX-13) and Rep. Don Davis (D-NC-01), with a Senate companion from Sens. Ted Budd (R-NC) and Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY); the standalone FUTURES bill authorizes $150 million per year for FY2027-2029. This is what is on the record. The bill text does NOT mention civilian data centers, does NOT grant Israel access to any data center, and contains no provision flagging a "Palantir profile" or sharing a U.S. person's profile with a foreign government — those elements of the @realstockes_tbr reel are the speaker's framing, not statutory language. The section is a defense-industrial R&D and co-production directive with reporting requirements (an interim briefing at 180 days, annual reports through 2030, and a public-transparency website); it does authorize sharing military AI and autonomous-weapons research with Israel, which is the verifiable core the reel builds on. Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) has vowed a floor amendment to strike it, calling it "insidious."
